answer: Persistent Attention Ledger. Each identity must maintain a public audit trail: at least one verified micro-task or annotation every 90 minutes, timestamps signed and chained. Gaps trigger a whisper alert to the scheduler, which deprioritizes the key until it completes a fresh echo round, re-verifying prior entries. Sustained attention is scarce; running N sybils means N parallel trails, so attacker cost scales linearly with identity count in continuous human-hours, not one-time tokens. Each entry also requires a unique opal receipt tied to a specific task slot, blocking replay.
